name: Dissolving sodium chloride in water

time_constant_s.source: teaching-pace timescale, not a measured rate

observations.started: The white crystals begin to dissolve.
observations.saturated: No more salt dissolves: the solution is saturated and crystals remain at the bottom.
observations.completed: All the salt has dissolved. The solution stays colourless.

explanation: Water molecules surround the sodium ions (Na⁺) and chloride ions (Cl⁻) and pull them out of the crystal. Dissolved ions are colourless, so the liquid looks the same as before.
